newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel wins transatlantic cable deal.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel wins transatlantic cable deal.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom said it had been awarded a two-billion franc contract for the supply of an advanced transatlantic fibre optic communications system, including two cables linking London and New York.

The contract has been awarded by Cable Co International Ltd, a vehicle through which MFS Communications Company Inc of the U.S. and Cable and Wireless Plc of Britain intend to enter into a joint venture to build, operate and own the system.
Alcatel said in a statement that the contract was the first to be awarded to a single supplier for the design, manufacture and installation of a system comprising two separate transoceanic cables.
It added it was also the first time that the commissioning of key elements of the land segment, and the end-to-end network management system have been included as part of an undersea system contract.
The new ring is scheduled for completion in 1998. The cable system will be in service in less than 15 months, which Alcatel called an "unprecedented" contract to service time.

The system will use synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) equipment and have a configuration with a 10 gigabit per second capacity which will be used for broadband services such as multimedia and Internet, as well as more traditional voice and data communication services.
Alcatel won the order through its Alcatel Submarine Networks subsidiary.
